### Subset to the samples I want to use with limma
## ENmix 
Reported to work good including batch effect correction.
https://genomebiology.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13059-022-02793-w

```{r}
df.failed.probes = read.csv(
  "../../results/01_pre_process/03_probes_QC/failed_probes/failed_probes.txt",
  header = FALSE
  )
failed.probes <- df.failed.probes$V1
print(length(failed.probes))
```

## MSet vs ENmix MSet
Now, I want to run preprocessENmix() using failed probes, the output should have similar dim as MSet manually filtered.

```{r}
print(dim(rp.sf.MSet))
```

```{r}
minfi::densityPlot(rp.sf.MSet)
```

```{r}
dim(sf.rgSet_ext)

ENmixMSet <-preprocessENmix(
  sf.rgSet_ext,# filtered out sample before
  bgParaEst = "oob",# background estimation
  dyeCorr = "RELIC",# dye bias correction
  nCores = 12,
  exCpG = failed.probes # add the failed probes to be excluded
)
print(dim(ENmixMSet))

save(
  ENmixMSet, 
  file = "../../results/01_pre_process/04_normalization/SetObjects/ENmixMSet.RData"
  )

```


# Approach 2: I can use BMIQ instead of the quantile, better normalization.

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(wateRmelon)
wtR.BMIQ.betas <- wateRmelon::BMIQ(ENmixMSet)

# Save
save(
  wtR.BMIQ.betas, 
  file = "../../results/01_pre_process/04_normalization/SetObjects/wtR_betas_norm_BMIQ.RData"
  )
dim(wtR.BMIQ.betas)
```
# At the end I didnt use this, I apply windsorization for extreme values

```{r eval=FALSE}
BMIQ.betas.norm.ftr = qcfilter(
  wtR.BMIQ.betas,
  rmoutlier = TRUE, 
  rmcr = TRUE, # remove col and row with too many missing values (default 5%)
  rthre = 0.05, #5% rows
  cthre = 0.05, #5% columns
  impute = FALSE
) #filter out low quality and outlier values, remove rows and cols

dim(BMIQ.betas.norm.ftr)
```

```{r}
norm.m.values = B2M(BMIQ.betas.norm.ftr)
boxplot(norm.m.values, main = "M-value distribution across samples")
```
# ENmix

```{r}
save(
  BMIQ.betas.norm.ftr, 
  file = "../../results/01_pre_process/04_normalization/SetObjects/wtR_BMIQ_betas_norm_ftr.RData"
  )
dim(BMIQ.betas.norm.ftr)
```



```{r}
betas <- BMIQ.betas.norm.ftr

ENmixMSet <- ENmixMSet[featureNames(ENmixMSet) %in% rownames(betas), ]

typeI <- getProbeInfo(ENmixMSet, type = "I")[, c("Name","nCpG")]
typeII <- getProbeInfo(ENmixMSet, type = "II")[, c("Name","nCpG")]

plot(
  density(
    rowMeans(
      betas[rownames(betas) %in% typeII$Name, ]),
      na.rm=T
      ),
    weights=rep(1/nrow(betas), sum(typeII$nCpG)),
     col="black",
  xlab="Beta",
  lwd=2,
  lty=2,
  main="Beta-value by type")

lines(
  density(
    rowMeans(
      betas[rownames(betas) %in% typeI$Name, ],      na.rm=T
      ),
    weights = rep(1 / sum(rownames(betas) %in% typeI$Name), 
                  sum(rownames(betas) %in% typeI$Name))
    ),
  col="black", lwd=2, lty=1)

```

## Approach 1 (I didnt use it in the final version): Normalize inter-array normalization
```{r eval=FALSE}
start.time <- Sys.time()
ENmixMSet.norm <- norm.quantile(ENmixMSet, method="quantile1")# Normalization
elapsed.time <- Sys.time() - start.time
print(elapsed.time)

save(
  ENmixMSet.norm,
  file = "../../results/01_pre_process/04_normalization/SetObjects/ENmixMSet_norm.RData"
)
densityPlot(ENmixMSet.norm)
```

```{r}
ENmix.beta.norm.rcp <- rcp(ENmixMSet.norm) # Regression on correlated probes
save(
  ENmix.beta.norm.rcp, 
  file = "../../results/01_pre_process/04_normalization/SetObjects/ENmix_beta_norm_rcp.RData"
  )
print(dim(ENmix.beta.norm.rcp))
```

## Convert the qcd and filtered MSet to grSet
```{r}
ratioSet <- ratioConvert(ENmixMSet.norm, what = "both", keepCN = TRUE)
grSet <- mapToGenome(ratioSet)

norm.grSet <- updateObject(grSet, beta=ENmix_betas.norm.ftr)
dim(norm.grSet)

# ENmix
save(
  norm.grSet, 
  file = "../../results/01_pre_process/04_normalization/SetObjects/ENmix_norm_ftr_grSet.RData"
  )
```

# Apply ENmix filtering 
For now I dont use this function, it is removing outlier by using Tukey's fences and imputing outliers by using knn. 

```{r eval=FALSE}
ENmix_betas.norm.ftr = qcfilter(
  ENmix.beta.norm.rcp,
  rmoutlier = TRUE, 
  byrow = TRUE,
  rmcr = TRUE, # remove col and row with too many missing values (default 5%)
  rthre = 0.05, #5% rows
  cthre = 0.05, #5% columns
  impute=TRUE # knn to impute
) #filter out low quality and outlier values, remove rows and cols

dim(ENmix_betas.norm.ftr)

# ENmix
save(
  ENmix_betas.norm.ftr, 
  file = "../../results/01_pre_process/04_normalization/SetObjects/ENmix_betas_norm_ftr.RData"
  )
dim(ENmix_betas.norm.ftr)
```
